kpis.name: S&P 500
kpis.note: Broad equity risk-on/risk-off signal. High VIX or S&P drawdown signals demand risk for Southwire construction end markets.

kpis.name: Brent Crude
kpis.note: Energy costs affect Southwire manufacturing and logistics. Sustained Brent >$90 pressures freight and resin input costs.

kpis.name: Copper (LME)
kpis.note: Primary raw material. Copper content of wire drives COGS. Sustained elevation compresses margin unless hedged or repriced.

kpis.name: Aluminum (LME)
kpis.note: Key input for aluminum wire and cable. Price signals secondary cost pressure and hedge calendar triggers.

kpis.name: Freight (Drewry WCI)
kpis.note: Ocean freight index drives import costs on raw materials and packaging. WCI >$4K signals elevated supply chain risk.
kpis.change: Monitor Drewry WCI weekly for rate momentum

kpis.name: VIX
kpis.note: Equity market fear gauge. VIX >25 indicates risk-off environment; monitor customer demand signals and receivables.

kpis.name: Natural Gas
kpis.note: Energy input for manufacturing and logistics. Sustained elevation pressures margin. Drives residential heating demand indirectly.

kpis.name: Gold
kpis.note: Risk sentiment indicator. Gold >$3,000 with VIX elevation signals macro uncertainty that may dampen CapEx spending by customers.

wire.title: Understanding the tech giants' oversized influence in American schools
wire.summary: Big tech companies like Apple and Microsoft use devices, training and conferences for teachers and students to embed in schools. The New York Times' Natasha Singer discusses the impact in Coding Kids.

wire.title: Iran fires on its Gulf neighbors, retaliating for U.S. strikes after a monthlong lull
wire.summary: The six-month war has led to a spike in oil prices, roiled the global economy and posed increasing political problems for President Trump's Republican Party ahead of November midterm elections.

wire.title: Greetings from the Royal Pavilion, a stunning reminder of India in southern England
wire.summary: Looking up at this 18th century building, it became clear the British didn't only bring their architectural style to India. They also took some of India's style home.

wire.title: Chevron to expand in Venezuela, days after the U.S. and Venezuela strike oil deal
wire.summary: Chevron is the largest foreign oil operator in Venezuela. The deal will expand its footprint at a time of political and economic uncertainty for Venezuela.

wire.title: Medical groups offer vaccine guidance to fill federal vacuum
wire.summary: In the unprecedented absence of federal guidance, leading medical groups are issuing their own recommendations for who should get the COVID-19, flu and RSV immunizations.

wire.title: New lawsuits claim OpenAI execs put image ahead of safety in Canadian mass shooting
wire.summary: The suits say that recommendations to alert police about the alleged shooter were nixed by OpenAI's global affairs team, led by veteran political strategist Chris Lehane. OpenAI denies the claims.

wire.title: Whatever happened to ... children infected with HIV due to failures in healthcare?
wire.summary: For years, Pakistan has seen cases of children infected with HIV due to unsafe treatment in clinics and hospitals. A current outbreak numbers hundreds of cases. Why does this problem keep occurring?

wire.title: India's prime minister is wooing the Gen Z while cracking down on them
wire.summary: Over two months, protesters, most who appeared to be digitally-savvy GenZ, used social media to organize. Government's efforts to respond spotlight how the ruling party appears to be playing catch-up.

wire.title: ICE says it now has enough body cameras. And, Congress averts shutdown before midterms
wire.summary: Immigration and Customs Enforcement says it now has enough body cameras to equip all of its agents. And, Congress votes to fund the government, averting a government shutdown ahead of the midterms.

wire.title: Israel bars U.S. citizens over criticism and ties to Palestinian activists, lawyers say
wire.summary: Travelers from the U.S. and other nations are denied entry to Israel after interrogations about their links to Palestinians, plans to visit the occupied West Bank and opinions of Israel, lawyers say.

wire.title: Iran says US strike killed four at wedding in 'war crime' as US denies targeting civilians
wire.summary: Iranian media reports two children were among those killed when shrapnel hit a home. Iran then launched missiles and drones at US targets in the Middle East.

wire.title: EU and Nato vow to step up pressure on Russia after 'new escalation' in Germany
wire.summary: Russia is accused of growing increasingly reckless after Berlin blamed Russia for a failed drone attack on Leipzig airport.

wire.title: Rosenberg: Putin's veiled threat to UK part of Russia's campaign against West
wire.summary: The Russian president wants to keep Britain guessing - and stressing - over Moscow's real intentions.

wire.title: US sailors arrive in Thailand's Pattaya after record 250 days at sea
wire.summary: The USS Abraham Lincoln is docking close to Pattaya, known for its neon-lit nightlife, and for sex tourism.

wire.title: Woman charged with juror intimidation in Lindsay Clancy trial
wire.summary: Dawn Light is accused of taking photos of jurors outside the Plymouth courthouse, a practice prohibited by the court.

wire.title: Zelensky says airlines should avoid Russian airspace as Ukraine escalates drone operations
wire.summary: Chinese and Gulf state airlines are among those still using Russian airspace. Meanwhile, Russia says it will intensify its own attacks on Ukraine.
